memory_update.text: FORM should be tracked as a direct HBM probe-card/test-intensity beneficiary; key survival tests are HBM probe-card revenue growth, capacity expansion, and customer breadth.
ONTO is not small-cap but has unusually direct HBM4 process-control evidence via Dragonfly G5 selection by a leading HBM manufacturer.
KLIC remains an underfollowed advanced-packaging bonding candidate; verify whether thermocompression bonding is material enough to change the company’s legacy wire-bonder profile.
COHU is a lower-attention HBM inspection/test-handler hypothesis; the key evidence gap is materiality of HBM inspection versus broader cyclical test exposure.

Need a later pass for materials and consumables such as underfill, thermal interface materials, substrates, glass carriers, and specialty chemicals; this pass emphasized US-listed direct equipment and process-control companies.
CAMT belongs in the HBM advanced-packaging second-layer universe as an inspection/metrology candidate with direct HBM, chiplet, and hybrid-bonding language in 2026 SEC and investor materials.
FORM belongs in the HBM second-layer universe as a probe-card/test candidate; strongest evidence to verify is HBM DRAM customer expansion and HBM4-related probe-card demand.
KLIC belongs in the HBM second-layer universe as a speculative-to-underfollowed bonding-equipment candidate; key survival test is whether first HBM system shipment converts to repeat revenue.
Inspection/metrology, probe cards, and bonding tools appear to be the most evidence-backed US-listed public-market mappings for HBM and advanced-packaging second-layer supplier exposure in this pass.

The useful underfollowed gap is not simply small market cap; it is mismatch between HBM qualification evidence and analyst/investor tendency to classify these companies as generic semiconductor equipment or test names.

FORM should be tracked as an HBM probe-card/test bottleneck candidate; key survival test is whether HBM probe-card demand remains allocation-constrained and margin-accretive rather than a one-quarter DRAM cycle effect.
CAMT is a direct advanced-packaging inspection/metrology candidate with AI OSAT order evidence; verify customer concentration and conversion of CoWoS-like/HBM demand into sustained segment revenue.
KLIC is a lower-attention bonding-equipment hypothesis; keep only if filings and calls confirm HBM/thermocompression bonding materiality, customer qualifications, and durable backlog.

ONTO is a $10B-$30B exception because HBM4 Dragonfly G5 selection and advanced-packaging process-control exposure are unusually direct; verify whether the HBM win broadens beyond one leading memory customer.

For HBM and advanced-packaging second-layer suppliers, the most relevant chokepoint subnodes in this pass are probe cards/wafer test, inspection/metrology, thermocompression or hybrid-bonding equipment, and process-control software/data attached to advanced packaging lines.

The underfollowed edge is likely not 'HBM exposure' broadly, which is now widely recognized, but names where HBM revenue is hidden inside probe-card mix, advanced-packaging tool shipments, OSAT orders, or customer qualification disclosures.
ONTO is the clean reference anchor for HBM advanced-packaging process control because management disclosed a multi-year HBM customer VPA for Dragonfly 2D/3D bump metrology.
FORM belongs in the underfollowed lane as an HBM probe-card/test candidate; the hidden KPI is HBM share of DRAM probe-card revenue and sustainability of probe-card demand as HBM capacity ramps.
CAMT is a strong underfollowed inspection/metrology candidate because its filings explicitly tie systems to advanced packaging, chiplets and HBM stack inspection.
KLIC should remain a hypothesis until primary filings or call transcripts confirm direct HBM, TCB, hybrid-bonding or AI packaging revenue rather than broad advanced-packaging cyclicality.

For HBM second-layer suppliers, the most testable sub-nodes are 2D/3D bump metrology, probe cards and wafer-level test, 100% stack inspection, thermocompression bonding, hybrid-bonding readiness, and advanced-packaging consumables/components.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the HBM/advanced-packaging second-layer supplier universe toward US-listed direct equipment, inspection, probe/test, and bonding suppliers. The most relevant underfollowed lane candidates are FormFactor, Kulicke & Soffa, and Cohu; Onto Innovation is included as a higher-attention reference/direct supplier because its HBM4 inspection and metrology exposure appears unusually direct. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list. Expanded the universe below obvious HBM producers into US-listed process-control, probe/test, inspection/metrology, and bonding equipment names. The cleanest Layer 1B candidates are not memory producers, but suppliers whose tools become more valuable as HBM layer counts, bump density, hybrid bonding, thermocompression bonding, and advanced-packaging inspection intensity rise. This pass intentionally excludes mega-cap AI leaders except as implicit demand anchors and keeps the focus on less-followed suppliers with verifiable HBM or advanced-packaging exposure. Expanded the HBM/advanced-packaging second-layer supplier universe toward US-listed, underfollowed or less-obvious process-control, probe/test, inspection/metrology, and bonding equipment names. Reference anchors remain HBM producers and advanced-packaging capacity owners such as Micron, SK hynix, Samsung, TSMC, and OSATs, but this pass focuses below them.
